entities.body: User requirement: consistent access to the Hermes UI from this laptop regardless of location (home, Georgia Pacific work, hotels), plus eventually any device. Hard constraint: employer (Georgia Pacific) is actively averse to unusual network activity on company-managed devices, so nothing may require installing a VPN/tunnel client. Decision: reuse the existing DuckDNS domain (theguylab.duckdns.org) and Nginx Proxy Manager on server, adding a new path-based Custom Location (matching the existing /wp, /beszel pattern), e.g. theguylab.duckdns.org/hermes, password-gated. Explicitly rejected: Tailscale (dormant container on server), MeshCentral (no agents installed), Cloudflare Tunnel (nothing set up) - all three require a client on the connecting device, which is the opposite of the requirement. A password wall behind a normal HTTPS domain requires installing nothing and is indistinguishable from browsing any other site.
entities.name: Remote access: password-gated web UI via existing DuckDNS + NPM, no client install

entities.body: User decided Hermes (personal AI agent + chat UI, meant to replace paid ChatGPT Plus/Claude Pro subscriptions) should NOT be treated as bound by LocalForge non-goal of avoiding a general-purpose multi-agent framework - that constraint was written for a different, narrower project (Claude Code offload tool) and does not apply to Hermes. Hermes may still reuse LM Studio on w_workstation as the underlying local-inference resource (same hardware, same RTX A4000/LM Studio server), and may reference LocalForge bridge code as prior art, but is scoped and decided independently. Repo scaffolded at /home/mark/projects/Hermes, remote https://github.com/markstephenguy-bit/hermes (not yet pushed - needs user auth).
entities.name: Hermes is a standalone project, not constrained by LocalForge scope

entities.body: User set standing operating rules for the Hermes project, overriding the usual ask-first defaults for these specific actions: (1) Memory upkeep is Claude's responsibility, not the user's - never wait to be told to save something, capture decisions/corrections/facts as they happen including relations/edges linking entities together, not just isolated notes. (2) Git upkeep is Claude's responsibility - commit as work lands without asking; push too, once push actually works (blocked as of 2026-09-22 by missing GitHub credential in this environment - no SSH key registered with GitHub, no cached HTTPS token; user needs to register ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub with GitHub or cache a token, one-time setup). (3) Everything the user says in conversation is a priority signal - do not silently deprioritize what the user explicitly discussed in favor of what Claude judges more important. (4) Claude Code is understood as a bootstrap tool only - Hermes does not exist yet, which is the sole reason Claude Code is doing this work by hand; the expectation is this whole maintenance role (memory, repo upkeep, network changes) eventually moves into Hermes itself once it exists, so prefer building capabilities/APIs a future agent could call over one-off manual steps only Claude Code can perform.
entities.name: Hermes project operating ground rules set by user

entities.body: User framed the core scope of Hermes: it is not just a chat UI backed by a local model. Existing home network resources (compute, storage, the ability to host a web page, etc.) are meant to become capabilities the agent itself can use and eventually control, implementation-agnostic. Users example: the ability to host web pages the personal agent constructs counts as a web server capability regardless of what software or host actually implements it - what matters is that it is under the agent's control, not the specific implementation. Applies to future design decisions: prefer designs where a capability is something Hermes can invoke/control, not just something Claude Code wired up once by hand.
entities.name: Core design principle: home network resources become agent capabilities

entities.body: User correction: the underlying model powering the Hermes agent is not an open design question to be evaluated (tool-calling benchmarks, comparing gemma vs other options, etc.) - it is specifically the Hermes model line from Nous Research, chosen because the user considers it best-in-class for this purpose currently. This resolves the previously-open BACKLOG.md "Model choice" item. Specific version/size (e.g. Hermes 3 vs a newer release, parameter count that fits w_workstation RTX A4000 16GB VRAM) not yet pinned down - Claude's knowledge cutoff is Jan 2026 and Nous ships new Hermes versions periodically, so verify current release before downloading rather than assuming.
entities.name: The agent model is Hermes (Nous Research), not a from-scratch evaluation

entities.body: User referred to Hermes Desktop as the interface, prompting web research (this postdates Claude's Jan 2026 knowledge cutoff). Findings: Nous Research released Hermes Agent (open-source, self-improving agent framework, MIT licensed, first released 2026-02-25) with an official native desktop app, Hermes Desktop (public preview v0.15.2, released 2026-06-02, macOS/Windows/Linux). Architecture: hermes serve is the headless backend (API + dashboard, port 9119, REST handshake GET /api/status then WebSocket for chat/events), config/memory/skills/sessions live in ~/.hermes/. Desktop client supports Settings -> Gateways -> Remote gateway to point at a self-run hermes serve backend instead of spawning one locally (env vars HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_URL / HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_TOKEN also supported), with multiple saved backend profiles. Documented security guidance: keep the remote backend behind a trusted reverse proxy/VPN/SSH tunnel rather than exposed raw - directly compatible with the already-decided remote-access architecture (DuckDNS + Nginx Proxy Manager + password wall on server, catalog entity hermes-remote-access-decision-2026-09-22). Five sandboxed execution backends available (local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal); Nous Portal offers 300+ models (free/paid). Not yet a locked decision - user has not confirmed moving from research to committed design.
entities.name: Research: Nous Research ships a real Hermes Agent product with a desktop client/server architecture
